question: A physicist trains the same next-item guessing architecture on gravity-wave readings instead of English text. Based on the lecture, what should she expect?

options.text: The model learns the structure of gravity-wave data the way it learns English
options.feedback: The learner is general-purpose: hide the next item, guess, adjust. Feed it English and it learns English; feed it gravity-wave data and it learns about gravity waves. Nothing in the method is specific to language.

options.text: The model fails, because the architecture was designed around words
options.feedback: The architecture is not built around words; it is built around predicting the next item in a sequence, whatever the items are. Words are just one kind of sequence.

options.text: The model needs a rulebook of physics loaded in before it can start
options.feedback: No rules are written down for English either. The whole point of self-supervised learning is that the data provides its own answer, so physics would be learned the same way.

options.text: The model translates the readings into English sentences before learning from them
options.feedback: Nothing gets translated. The readings become numbers the model predicts directly; there is no English step in between.
